text:
alex: Hey team — ACME (tenant acme-retail) opened a ticket: their API calls to our hosted endpoint are being routed to us-west which adds ~250ms and causes token validation failures. They say their VPC + private deployment is in eu-central. Can we triage?
priya: Can you paste the customer headers and a small repro curl? Also need the ARN/tenant ID.
alex: Tenant: acme-retail, sample curl from their on-prem BF box:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response shows 403 + huge RTT. Response headers include: `x-rw-proxied-region: us-west-2`, `x-rw-egress-ip: 54.201.12.7`
emma: They claim their TGW/VPC peering endpoints are all in eu-central and routes look correct on their side. They see traffic leaving via a peered hub in eu but our logs disagree.
jordan: Can you share a traceroute and the customer's route table attachment for the peering? Also include our private egress proxy healthcheck logs around the times.
alex: Traceroute attached in ticket (pasted below):
```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.com (54.201.12.7), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.234 ms  0.211 ms  0.200 ms
 5  100.65.2.1 (100.65.2.1)  12.45 ms  12.40 ms  12.50 ms
 8  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  120.1 ms 120.0 ms 119.9 ms
 9  54.201.12.7 (54.201.12.7)  250.8 ms 250.7 ms 250.9 ms
```
priya: That external hop 203.0.113.45 looks like a transit peer in our asia-exchange — odd. Can you also fetch the customer's NAT gateway IPs and the peering route priorities?
alex: Customer NAT IPs: 198.51.100.12 (eu egress) and 198.51.100.13 (backup). Their VPC route table shows `0.0.0.0/0 -> tg-w-attach (preference 100)` and peering -> transit-gw-eu (preference 90).
priya: Hmm route preferences seem fine. On our side, the private egress controller uses proxy-service affinity + health-based weighting. If the eu proxy reports degraded health, our smart-router can fall back to next-region proxy (us-west) for latency/SLA reasons. Need healthcheck history.
eng-oncall-bot: [incident] private-egress-proxy-eu-central health degraded 2025-10-14T09:12:01Z -> 09:17:22Z (5m21s). Failover activated to us-west-2 for affected tenants.
jordan: There — failover window. Why did health degrade? Could be transient kernel OOMs on proxy host, or circuit-level packet loss from peering. Can we pull metrics: connection errors, proxy 502/504 counts, and iptables drops for that timeframe?
alex: I pulled proxy logs: frequent TLS handshake timeouts, followed by 502 responses. Sample snippet:
```
[2025-10-14T09:13:05Z] INFO connection from 198.51.100.12:52344 -> accepted
[2025-10-14T09:13:06Z] WARN TLS handshake timeout after 10s
[2025-10-14T09:13:06Z] ERROR upstream connect failed: i/o timeout
[2025-10-14T09:13:06Z] RETURN 502 proxied to us-west-2
```
priya: That suggests the eu proxy couldn't reach the upstream model routers (maybe a peering flake). The router then marked eu as unhealthy and our global routing policy rerouted traffic to us-west which explains the wrong-region selection and token rejection (aud claim mismatch expected region).
emma: Customer sees billing anomalies (requests counted under us-west pool) and auth failures. They're asking for remediation steps and an RCA.
jordan: Short-term: revert traffic to eu by forcing tenant affinity to preferred-region for acme-retail while we heal. I can push a policy override to pin them to eu-central for 30m. Also create a rollback if eu remains unhealthy.
alex: I'll open a support incident and notify customer. Emma — can you confirm if forcing region will impact their throughput SLA?
emma: I'll confirm with the account team; quick heads-up to customer that we will pin them to eu for now.
priya: Longer-term: need better heartbeat routes from peering to detect peering-level packet loss so proxy doesn't mark region unhealthy prematurely. Also add a token-audience-fallback so auth checks don't fail when region-mapped aud differs (or avoid changing aud on failover).
jordan: Agreed. Action items: 1) alex — notify customer & collect customer NAT tcpdump. 2) priya — postmortem on eu proxy health, uplink packet drops, and increase healthcheck hysteresis. 3) jordan — policy override to pin tenant for 30m and monitor. 4) eng — consider making aud region-agnostic on fallback.
alex: Noted. Customer notified in ticket; they provided tcpdump and say traffic shows retransmits. I'll attach.
emma: Thanks. I'll also log a billing adjustment request for counts during the failover window.
eng-oncall-bot: [task] policy-override applied to tenant acme-retail: region=eu-central ttl=1800s by jordan
priya: I'll dig into peering metrics and get back with root cause in ~2 hours.
alex: Closing loop here once we have the postmortem. :thumbsup:
